title: Staggered release playbook for hybrid-inference features (WIP)
content:
Context and purpose:

This is a working playbook for launching inference features that touch multiple infra modes at once: hosted API, Dedicated pools, and Private (VPC/on-prem). We call this a "hybrid-inference" rollout because the feature surfaces and model variants will be served across different deployment types and capacity tiers. The goal is to provide an operationally lightweight but safe path for progressive exposure while preserving cost/latency SLOs and minimizing blast radius.

Why a separate playbook?
- Existing canary and AB playbooks assume a single deployment plane. Hybrid launches add combinatorial complexity: model variant x infra mode x quantization x routing policy.
- We need clear stepwise exposure that reasons about resource constraints (GPU pools), fallback chains, and cross-team coordination (platform, product, SRE, solutions).

Key principles (short)
- Keep the blast radius minimal: start small on the narrowest dimension (usually infra mode or user cohort).
- Measure orthogonal signals: correctness/quality (evals), infra signals (latency/p95, GPU saturation), and economic signals (tokens/millisecond cost).
- Enforce deterministic fallback and a single source-of-truth toggle per audience slice.
- Communicate expected rollback conditions before starting.

Stakeholders and roles
- Release owner: product engineer (single point of contact for go/no-go).
- Platform lead: config and routing changes (traffic rules, model pins).
- SRE on-call: infra safety, scaling, paging.
- Observability lead: dashboards and alerts for the run.
- Solutions / Customer success: for any customer-facing anomalies.

Launch dimensions (pick an ordering for staging)
1) Model variant (v1 float32 -> v2 quantized)
2) Infra plane (hosted -> dedicated -> private)
3) Traffic cohort (internal employees -> pilot customers -> 1% public -> ramp)
4) Feature gatefulness (prefetching, caching enabled)

Suggested staging sequence (conservative)
- Stage 0: internal canary - dev team + product + SRE traffic only. Model pinned on hosted test instance. No customer-facing traffic.
- Stage 1: infra orthogonalization - deploy model to a dedicated pool and to a Private test tenant (if relevant) but keep routing off. Run synthetic/record-replay traffic for 1–2 hours and collect perf + regression metrics.
- Stage 2: internal beta cohort - route 0.5% internal + selected power users. Enable live routing to hosted and dedicated variants concurrently (split by header). Watch for cross-variant discrepancies.
- Stage 3: pilot customers - route to 5 pilot customers (can be on dedicated/private) with explicit SLOs and escalation contacts.
- Stage 4: public micro-release - 1% random traffic across hosted; monitor 30m windows for stability, then progressive increase to 10%/25%/100% with checkpoints.

Traffic partitioning patterns (examples)
- By header: X-Release-Variant: control | hybrid-v2
- By route: dedicated-only for resource-heavy routes, hosted for low-latency short requests
- By user cohort: pro-plan customers directed to Dedicated for predictable latency; free-tier stays on hosted.

Gating signals (stop/rollback thresholds) - define before launch
Quality signals (per prompt set)
- Regression rate on eval suite > 2x baseline
- Human-rated correctness drop > 3 points (on our 100-point rubric)

Infra signals
- p95 latency increase > 2x baseline for more than 10 minutes
- GPU util sustained > 85% for more than 5 minutes on Dedicated pools
- Error rate (5xx) spike above 1% absolute or 3x relative baseline

Cost signals
- Per-token unit cost increase > 25% vs expected for the deployment mix

Operational run cadence (during every active ramp)
- 0–30m: minute-by-minute check-ins for first 10m, then 5m cadence until stable
- 30–120m: 15-minute cadence
- >120m: hourly check-ins until fully ramped
- Async status updates posted to #rollouts with runbook template filled every cadence tick

Pre-launch checklist (must complete before Stage 1)
- Toggle creation: single feature flag / release-id controlling routing logic.
- Dashboard: baseline dashboards cloned with new variant filters (latency, errors, cost, model-quality).
- Canary eval set: curated prompt set (50–200 prompts) representing critical user journeys.
- Synthetic traffic harness configured for dedicated/private test pools.
- Fallback chain documented: model variant -> fallback model (compatible architecture) -> degrade to cached response.
- Communication: scheduled stakeholder kickoff + rollback email template.

Observability specifics (what to instrument)
- Token-level cost logs (token_count, model_variant, infra_plane)
- KV cache hit ratio and prefix-caching effectiveness for each pool
- Model output divergence metric: pairwise edit distance + key-entity drift for rerankers
- Traces sampled at 10% for high-latency flows (capture sequence length, batching delay)

Example quick commands (ops)
- Toggle routing (pseudo): curl -X POST $CONSOLE/api/releases/12345/toggle -d '{"variant":"hybrid-v2","state":"on","scope":"pilot-cust-list"}'
- Revert routing: curl -X POST $CONSOLE/api/releases/12345/toggle -d '{"variant":"hybrid-v2","state":"off"}'

Fallback policy template (must be enacted automatically)
- On host error threshold breach -> route to dedicated variant if health good
- If dedicated overloaded -> route to cached responses or a smaller-capacity float model
- If both fail -> degrade to message: "We're experiencing temporary service delays. Try again in a minute." (very rare; ensure product PM approved)

Communication plan (public & internal)
- Internal: start-of-run thread, hourly updates in #rollouts, immediate pager pages if any gating signal triggers.
- Pilot customers: hands-on email and optional conference call; provide diagnostic logs and intended mitigation timeline.
- Broader public: staged release notes once 10%+ stable, mention possible short-term tweaks.

Mini-runbook (one-page quick reference)
- Owner: <name> (pager)
- Start time: <ISO>
- Initial exposure: hosted-only, 0.5% (internal) for 30m
- Primary dashboards: Release XYZ perf + Quality heatmap
- Stop conditions: any gating signal (list) met
- Rollback steps: toggle off variant -> roll to fallback model -> notify stakeholders

Open questions / decision points (TODOs)
- How strictly do we enforce cost thresholds for private customers who prepay? (Need legal/finance input)
- Can we automate re-routing from dedicated -> hosted during transient GPU pressure without violating tenant isolation? (platform design)
- Sampling approach for human quality checks: can we recruit external annotators for live-run checks or rely on internal reviewers?

Notes from last dry-run (2025-10-15)
- Observability gaps: cache-miss metric not surfaced per-tenant; caused confusion when dedicated seemed slower. Action: add per-tenant cache metrics to dashboards.
- Miscommunication: rollout owner changed routing rule mid-run. Action: enforce single-author toggle policy.

Appendix: quick templates
- Rollout start message (copy/paste):
  "Starting hybrid-inference rollout: release=hybrid-v2, scope=pilot-customers, initial-exposure=5%, owner=Marisol Vega. Stop on any gating signal (listed). Pager: on-call SRE."
- Rollback message:
  "Rolling back hybrid-v2 -> control. Observed [reason]. Fallback in place: control-model-v1. Notifying pilot customers."

End notes:
This doc is intentionally informal; capture actions here and we will extract a trimmed runbook after first successful public roll. If you are an owner assigned to a stage, write your stage checklist as a subdocument and link it here (confluence / PR).

Related docs to update after completion:
- infra capacity playbook (add dedicated pool sizing rules)
- customer comms templates (pilot and public)

Last edits: added cost gating detail and the synthetic harness checklist.
